findings.F1: The bars just after the forecast turns positive lose money: in the first 20 days of a long stretch the book's mean daily return is -0.000512 (Sharpe -0.34, n=2065) and the coin's is -0.000471, against 0.000993 for days 20–60 (n=3524) and 0.001657 for days 60–120 (n=2619, Sharpe 0.90); the weak forecast bucket 0–5 also earns -0.000011 a day (n=2154).
findings.F2: While long, the coin's own past 20-day return grades what follows: in the top quintile (above +18.9%) the book earns 0.002455 a day (Sharpe 1.52, n=1731) and the coin 0.005509 (t 3.69); in the middle quintile the book earns 0.000157 and in the bottom quintile 0.000102.
findings.F3: While long, bars near the coin's 60-day high (within 3.4%) earn the book 0.001762 a day (Sharpe 1.11, n=1881); the other drawdown quintiles earn between -0.000125 and 0.001094.
findings.F4: The deepest falls happen while the book is long: BTC fell -45.6% in 88 days while fully long (share long 1.00, mean forecast 15.2, coin -63%). ZEC fell -84.8%, XRP -59.6% and ETH -69.1%, with the book long 61–75% of those stretches and the coin falling 71–92%. This is what keeps Calmar at 0.20.
findings.F5: Holding beats the book because the flat bars still carry the coin's drift: on the 8454 bars with forecast 0 the coin averages 0.001295 a day (t 2.79) while the book earns 0.000018. Every coin's book mean (0.000108–0.000868) is below its coin mean (0.000670–0.001879).
findings.F6: The volatility sizing puts the smallest positions where the coin gains most: in the highest 20-day volatility quintile the coin earns 0.004961 a day (t 2.89) at a mean allocation of 0.33, while the lowest quintile earns 0.000591 at an allocation of 0.67.
findings.F7: Fees are not the cause: 905 trades average 5.64% gross and 5.54% net, with a mean commission of 0.11%, a median length of 39 days and 37% winners.

ideas.idea: While a coin's 50-day SMA is above its 200-day SMA, the coin keeps rising, further the larger the spread, only while its own recent return is strongly positive and its price stands near its recent high; the stronger the recent rise, the larger the gain that follows.
ideas.consequence: A trader would hold the golden-cross long in proportion to the coin's recent momentum and refuse it when price stalls or drops away from its high inside the cross.
ideas.name: golden cross with momentum

ideas.idea: While a coin's 50-day SMA is above its 200-day SMA, the coin keeps rising, further the larger the spread, except in the early stretch just after the cross; the drift grows with the time the short average has stayed above the long one.
ideas.consequence: A trader would scale into a golden-cross long as the cross ages, rather than buying the fresh cross.
ideas.name: aged cross drift

ideas.idea: While a coin's 50-day SMA is above its 200-day SMA, the coin's upward drift is larger the higher its recent daily volatility.
ideas.consequence: A trader would not shrink the golden-cross position in volatile stretches, since those stretches carry most of the gain.
ideas.name: volatile trends drift further

ideas.idea: After a coin has risen strongly over its recent weeks, it keeps rising over the following days, and the larger the past rise, the larger the next rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader would go long in proportion to the coin's recent return, including while its averages have not yet crossed, which takes in the drift the cross book misses when flat.
ideas.name: recent rise keeps rising
